newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares dip in hesitant market.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares dip in hesitant market.

text.p: Sweden's stock exchange slipped on Thursday in a hesitant market after posting gains most of the day, buoyed by central bank cuts in key interest rates.
The Stockholm general index dipped 0.10 percent to 2139.40 after shares worth 3.3 billion crowns were traded.
The performance across the board was mixed.
"The market is extraordinarily cowardly just now," said one broker. "Noone is prepared to stick their chin out."
The release of nine month reports has started in Sweden with bearings maker SKF and forestry group Stora posting their earnings on Thursday which were much in line with expectations.
SKF closed 4.5 crowns lower at 154 crowns as it result was seen as disappointing. It reported a profit after financial items of 1.85 billion crowns versus market expectations of 1.9 billion crowns.
Stora rose 0.5 to 86 crowns after posting a drop in profit after financial items to 1.92 billion crowns from 6.19 billion a year ago. The market consensus was 1.89 billion crowns.
Bluechips were higher with telecoms giant Ericsson rising two to 182.5 crowns and drugs major Astra rising 0.5 to 306.5 crowns.
The bank sector index dipped 0.53 percent.

The central bank, Riksbank, lowered it key lending and deposit rates by 50 basis points to 5.75 percent and 4.25 percent respectively. It announced a 25 basis point in the repo rate to 4.60 percent next Tuesday.
Mining company Trelleborg was due to release its nine month report on Friday.
